title: AT&T bows to pressure from activist investor Elliott, CEO will stay on through 2020
主要内容: AT&T (T) announced plans to add two new board members and sell up to $10 billion in non-core businesses next year, responding to pressure from activist investor Elliott Management. The company also aims to pay off all debt from the Time Warner acquisition. Elliott Management, which holds a $3.2 billion stake, has been urging cost cuts and management changes. AT&T expects CEO Randall Stephenson to remain through at least 2020. The strategic plan was supported by Elliott, which praised the steps for creating shareholder value. AT&T reported third-quarter revenue of $44.59 billion, below analysts' estimate of $45 billion. Excluding items, it earned 94 cents per share, above the 93 cents expected. The company reduced net debt by $12.7 billion this year and expects to generate $14 billion through asset sales. It sold Puerto Rico assets to Liberty Latin America for $1.95 billion and plans to exit CME ownership through a $2.1 billion deal. AT&T added 101,000 net new phone subscribers, exceeding Wall Street's estimate of 61,000. Shares rose slightly to $37.50 pre-market.
